name: Cardpack Cultivation (卡包修仙)
tagline: A Chinese-language mobile game that mashes card pack opening, xianxia cultivation progression and light card battles into one idle loop.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. App Store listings of this type usually monetize through in-app purchases rather than a subscription.

verdictSummary: Mechanically this is one of the easiest things on this site to rebuild: weighted random draws, a pity counter, a collection grid, a currency that ticks up while you are away, and a battle resolver that compares numbers. An agent will hand you a working local version in an afternoon and you will open your first ten-pack within the hour. What it will not hand you is the part that makes the app worth opening twice: a few hundred hand-drawn cards with names, flavor text and tiers that feel deliberate, plus the pack-opening animation timing that turns a random number into a small event. Games are a genre where the tuning is the product, and tuning is not something you one-shot. Build it if you want to feel the loop or study the math; do not expect to want to play it next week.
coreLoopDIY: A local browser game that spends currency on card packs, rolls rarities against a weighted table with a pity counter, stores your collection, and runs simple auto-battles between decks.
requirements: Card art or placeholder glyphs of your own, since you cannot ship someone else's card illustrations
Willingness to invent your own rarity tiers, names and balance numbers
whatYouLose: The card art and the cultivation-flavored writing, which is most of what you are actually collecting
Animation and sound timing on the pack reveal, the entire reason gacha feels like anything
A progression curve someone actually playtested, instead of numbers an agent guessed at
Content updates: new packs, seasons, events, whatever keeps the loop alive past week one
Phone-native feel: offline play, notifications, haptics, and it living on your home screen
moatNotes: The mechanics are public domain in practice. The card set, the naming and the reveal choreography are the asset, and none of it comes out of a prompt.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays for a weighted random number generator. They pay because someone drew several hundred cards, wrote cultivation-flavored names for them, decided which ones feel rare, and spent months getting the pack-opening beat to land. Free replicas of gacha simulators exist by the dozen and they mostly feel hollow within twenty minutes, which is the honest measure of how much of this genre is content and polish rather than code.
notes: Rebuilding a gacha loop teaches you exactly how cheap the mechanic is and exactly how expensive the feeling is.
prompt:
Build a local, single-player card pack opening game that runs entirely in the browser. No backend, no accounts, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, Zustand for state, all save data in localStorage under one versioned key. No server, no external API calls, no asset downloads.

Game content: define a data file with 60 cards across 5 rarities (Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary). Each card has id, name, rarity, attack, defense, and one line of flavor text. Invent original xianxia-flavored names yourself, do not copy any existing game's card list. Represent art with a single emoji or unicode glyph per card plus a rarity-colored gradient frame; no image files.

Core loop:
- A currency called Spirit Stones that accrues at a fixed rate per second, calculated from elapsed wall-clock time since last save, so it works offline.
- A shop with one pack type: 10 cards for a fixed price. Rarity weights are constants in one config object, easy to edit.
- A pity counter: guarantee at least one Epic or better every 10 packs, tracked and displayed.
- A pack opening screen that reveals cards one at a time on click, with a CSS animation whose duration scales with rarity, and a distinct flourish for Legendary.
- A collection grid showing owned cards, duplicate counts, and locked silhouettes for cards not yet pulled.
- Duplicates convert to a second currency used to level a card, raising its attack and defense.

Battles: pick 5 cards for a deck, fight a generated opponent deck at your power tier. Resolution is deterministic, turn-by-turn, highest attack trades first, log each step as text. Winning pays Spirit Stones. Keep the combat math in one pure function with unit tests via Vitest.

Also include: a stats panel showing total packs opened, pulls per rarity, and your actual observed drop rates versus the configured ones. A reset button behind a confirm dialog.

Out of scope: multiplayer, trading, real money, sound, mobile builds, server sync.

Deliver a README with npm install, npm run dev, and a short paragraph on where to edit the rarity weights and card list.
